text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- An agrement between the doctor's association and the goverment exempts doctors from regulation on overtime work. The Labour Directorate complains the agreement allows doctors to work as much as they want to and that this could involve a risk for patients.

- This year Norwegian companies will spend 30 million crowns on advertising on the Internet, according to estimates by Knut-Arne Futsaeter, head of research in Norsk Gallup Institutt AS. Futsaeter says he expects the advertising to increase to several hundred millions crowns in a few years.

- The World Jewish Congress meets in Oslo to discuss restitution of Jewish property confiscated by the Nazis during the Holocaust in European countries, including Switzerland. Norway is held out as a model of cooperation by the Jews.
- Per-Kristian Foss, financial spokesman for the conservative party, wants the Oslo Bourse to turn into a listed company. Oslo Bourse is the only bourse in the Nordic that is not listed.
- The Centre Party says Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen should resign because of alleged irregularities in a share-option transaction in 1987.
